chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu 'Abdillah (عليه السلام), and a man complained to him (عليه السلام) of his needs. So he (عليه السلام) said to him: 'Be patient, for Allah would soon Make a relief for you.' He (the narrator) said: 'Then he (عليه السلام) remained silent for a while, then turned towards the man and said: "Inform me about the prison of Al-Kufa — how is it?" So he said: "May Allah Keep you well (عليه السلام)! It is narrow, fetid, and its inhabitants are in the worst of conditions." He (عليه السلام) said: "So you are indeed in the prison, and you are wanting to be in spaciousness within it? Do you not know that the world is a prison for the believer (al-mu'min)?"'

key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: the world, worldly life — framed by the Imam as a prison for the believer
key_terms.الْحَاجَةَ: need, want, or poverty — the material and financial hardship the man brought before the Imam
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنِ: the believer, al-mu'min — the one for whom this world is a place of trial and constriction
key_terms.سَعَةٍ: spaciousness, ease, amplitude — what the man implicitly sought while dwelling in worldly constraint
key_terms.سِجْنُ: prison — used by the Imam as a metaphor for the world and its inherent constriction
key_terms.ضَيِّقٌ: narrow, constricted — describing the physical state of the Kufa prison and, by analogy, the world for the believer
key_terms.فَرَجاً: relief, opening, or deliverance — the divine ease Allah (azwj) grants after hardship
key_terms.مُنْتِنٌ: fetid, putrid, foul-smelling — a characterization of the prison of Al-Kufa

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq (AS) say about the world being a prison for the believer?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates an exchange between Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (عليه السلام) and a man who lamented his poverty and material need. The Imam first counseled sabr (patience), then drew a pointed analogy between the physical prison of Al-Kufa — narrow, fetid, and wretched — and the world itself, revealing that this life is inherently a place of constriction and hardship for the believer. The tradition thus frames worldly difficulty not as an anomaly to be escaped, but as the very nature of this life for the faithful, demanding patience and proper perspective rather than complaint.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Ajlan who said,

‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullahasws, and a man complained to himasws of his needs. So heasws said to him: ‘Be patient, from Allahazwj would soon Make a relief to be for you’. He (the narrator) said, ‘Then heasws remained silent for a while, then turned towards the man and heasws said: ‘Inform me about the prison of Al-Kufa, how is it?’ So he said, ‘May Allahazwj Keep youasws well! Narrow, smelly, and its inhabitants are in an evil state’. Heasws said: ‘So rather, you are in the prison, and you are wanting that you happen to be capacious in it? Do you not know that the world is a prison for the Momin?’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn ‘Ajlan who has said the following: “

Once I was in the presence of abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) when a man complained to him about something he needed. The Imam said, ‘Be patient, Allah will make a way out for you.’ The narrator has said that he remained quiet for a while then he turned to the man and said, ‘Tell me about the jail in Kufah, how is it?’ The man said, ‘May Allah keep you well, it is congested, foul smelling and people are in the worst condition.’ The Imam said, ‘You are in a jail and expect comfort. You should bear in mind that this world is a prison for believing people’”
